subject.title: Orphaned lock files not cleared on gateway restart when PID matches current process

question: Should OpenClaw reclaim live current-PID session locks beyond untracked matching-starttime cleanup, or preserve them until a stronger owner/heartbeat signal proves they are stale?
rationale: This choice affects transcript integrity: reclaiming too broadly can cut off an active writer, while preserving too much leaves real channel sessions wedged behind the gateway's own lock.

options.title: Keep Focused Tracker
options.body: Keep this issue open for same-PID restart/recovery lock semantics while narrower PRs handle compaction, delivery, and timeout subcases.

options.title: Move Remaining Work
options.body: Close only after maintainers explicitly redirect the live current-PID behavior to a canonical open issue and preserve this thread's field evidence there.

options.title: Declare Boot Slice Done
options.body: Treat the startup cleanup slice as handled and open a new narrower issue for runtime/recovery live current-PID leaks.

recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for same-PID restart/recovery lock semantics while narrower PRs handle compaction, delivery, and timeout subcases.
